report.source_text: The MRI of the thoracic spine with IV contrast revealed widespread osseous metastatic neoplasm, with significant involvement in the mid-thoracic spine, centered around T7. This region shows an enhancing mass extending into the posterior mediastinum and prevertebral soft tissues, potentially contiguous with the esophagus, suggesting a primary neoplasm. Additionally, there is a pathologic fracture of the T7 vertebral body with erosion into the anterior epidural space, causing spinal canal narrowing. Dural thickening is observed cranially and caudally from this region along the thoracic spine over a 12 cm span, roughly from T4 to T9 (Figures 1-2).

report.source_text: Consultation with neurosurgery was sought, with their recommendation for surgical intervention; however, the patient declined after a thorough review of potential surgical complications. Instead, the patient opted for palliative radiotherapy, receiving a cumulative dose of 3000 cGy delivered in 10 fractions. This regimen involved external beam radiation with conformal treatment utilizing 18 mV photons with two fields, anterior and posterior, and was well-tolerated with no significant adverse effects reported.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Stage II multiple myeloma with kappa light chain restriction and biopsy-proven bone plasmacytoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 1.5-month history of progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness, numbness, and mid-lower back pain, culminating in impaired ambulation and a fall. Physical examination revealed severe bilateral lower extremity weakness (1/5) with intact upper extremity strength (5/5) and paraspinal tenderness throughout the spine. Imaging studies (CT chest and MRI thoracic spine) revealed widespread osseous metastatic disease with numerous lytic lesions throughout the spine and pelvis, a pathologic fracture of the T7 vertebral body with anterior epidural extension causing spinal canal narrowing and dural thickening over a 12 cm span (T4-T9). Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated monoclonal kappa plasma cell infiltrates (~12% of marrow cells), and biopsy of the T7 midthoracic mass confirmed a monoclonal kappa light chain-restricted plasmacytoma. final.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 1.5-month history of progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness, numbness, and mid-lower back pain, culminating in impaired ambulation and a fall. Physical examination revealed severe bilateral lower extremity weakness (1/5) with intact upper extremity strength (5/5) and paraspinal tenderness throughout the spine. Imaging studies (CT chest and MRI thoracic spine) revealed widespread osseous metastatic disease with numerous lytic lesions throughout the spine and pelvis, a pathologic fracture of the T7 vertebral body with anterior epidural extension causing spinal canal narrowing and dural thickening over a 12 cm span (T4-T9). Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated monoclonal kappa plasma cell infiltrates (~12% of marrow cells), and biopsy of the T7 midthoracic mass confirmed a monoclonal kappa light chain-restricted plasmacytoma. Flow cytometry showed aberrant monocyte expression (CD2, CD56). The patient was treated with intravenous fluids, calcitonin administered intramuscularly every 12 hours, and dexamethasone 4 mg every 6 hours, resulting in normalization of calcium levels and significant improvement in lower extremity weakness with restored mobility via physical therapy. The patient declined surgical intervention recommended by neurosurgery and instead received palliative radiotherapy (3000 cGy in 10 fractions using external beam radiation with conformal treatment), which was well-tolerated without significant adverse effects.
